The 287th Hunter Exam.name: The 287th Hunter Exam
The 287th Hunter Exam.description: Among thousands of desperate candidates in Zaban City's exam tunnel, you stand badge-less and untested as Satotz announces the beginning. Tonpa's poisoned juice circulates nearby. The real trials are about to start—survive if you can.
The 287th Hunter Exam.storyStart: The Underground Hall beneath Zaban City thrums with compressed energy. Three thousand candidates press against stone walls, their breathing echoing in a cavernous space lit by sputtering lamps. The air is thick with sweat and desperation. Each candidate wears a numbered badge—a necessity for the first trial. Yours feels heavy around your neck, a weight more psychological than physical. You scan the crowd. Some candidates are old hands, returning for a fourth or fifth attempt. Others are wide-eyed newcomers, barely concealing their fear. The examiner, a gaunt man named Satotz, stands on a raised platform. He has not smiled since he began speaking forty minutes ago. His words come methodically: proceed through the tunnel into Milsy Wetlands, reach the end alive, and you advance. "Cheating is permitted," he said. "Killing is not—but death may occur regardless." Somewhere in this crowd, Tonpa, the legendary Rookie Crusher, is watching. You've heard rumors: he targets newcomers with poisoned tea, theft, and sabotage. You've also heard he's a coward beneath his scheming. Behind you, an old man with a scarred face mutters to no one in particular about his seventh attempt. To your left, a nervous young man checks and rechecks his badge number. Around you, the ambient anxiety is sharp enough to cut. Satotz begins to descend from the platform. Within moments, the crowd will surge forward. The tunnel ahead is dark. The wetlands are said to be crawling with predators the Association imports specifically for the Exam. This moment—standing here, knowing what comes next—is your last moment of relative calm before everything changes.
The 287th Hunter Exam.questGenerationGuidance: The 287th Hunter Exam arc centers on surviving five brutal trials: the tunnel run through Milsy Wetlands (evasion and resource management), the tower (logic and ethical compromise), the badge hunt on Zevil Island (combat and survival), and the final tournament. Early-arc quests are about adaptation and raw survival. Encounters should emphasize camaraderie and competition between candidates, with Tonpa as a recurring social antagonist. The revelation of Nen should remain a rumor or legend—unconfirmed, whispered about by veteran candidates who claim to have seen "aura techniques." Examiner encounters are brief and impersonal; Satotz is correct but not merciful. The tower's "majority rules" voting floor introduces moral ambiguity and betrayal as mechanics.

Kukuroo Mountain.name: Kukuroo Mountain
Kukuroo Mountain.description: The Testing Gate looms before you—a stone archway that tourists claim no outsider has ever passed. Killua is somewhere beyond it, held by his family. The Zoldyck butlers regard you with polite hostility.
Kukuroo Mountain.storyStart: Kukuroo Mountain rises steeply from the forested landscape, its slopes covered in a gnarled canopy that seems to resist the sky. The air grows noticeably colder as you climb. The Tourist Bus Stop—a modest platform built into the mountainside—is where Zebro, the gatekeeper, checks your papers with bureaucratic precision. He is old, weathered, and unsurprised to see you. "Going to the Testing Gate?" he asks, though he already knows the answer. The gate itself becomes visible as you continue the path upward—an immense stone archway carved into the mountainside, inscribed with glyphs in a language older than living memory. A bronze plaque beside it reads: "ZOLDYCK FAMILY ESTATE. UNAUTHORIZED ENTRY FORBIDDEN." Behind the gate, you can see nothing but a winding path disappearing into shadow. To either side of the gate, mountain slope rises sheer and impassable. There is no climbing around it. A butler you would later learn is named Gotoh emerges from the shadow beyond the gate. He wears formal black livery despite being in a remote mountain compound. His face is ageless and controlled. "You wish entry?" he says, his tone suggesting he already knows the answer will be no. Beside you, if you've brought companions, they sense the sudden pressure in the air—the undeniable presence of trained Nen users. The Testing Gate before you displays numerical markings carved into its surface. Tourists speak of impossible weights attached to the gates. More truthfully: the gate responds to bloodline and training. You have neither. Behind you, the path downward is clear. Ahead, the gate bars everything.
Kukuroo Mountain.questGenerationGuidance: The Zoldyck arc is shorter but densely mechanical. Candidates advance by either: (1) training until they can legitimately open increasingly weighted doors, (2) finding non-confrontational paths (negotiation with butlers, finding servant shortcuts, leveraging social connections), or (3) proving worthiness in combat against butlers without lethal force. Killua's internal conflict is central—he wants to leave but fears his family. The butlers (Gotoh, Canary, Tsubone, Amane) are skilled Nen users who serve the family but harbor doubts. Canary's "Butler's Dilemma" is a side-quest introducing moral complexity into a coercive family structure. Silva, the patriarch, respects strength and determination; his eventual bargain (Killua may leave if he swears to return when his adventure is complete) rewards players who prove themselves without betraying their companions.

Heavens Arena.name: Heavens Arena
Heavens Arena.description: The 251-floor tower rises before you, its brass and stone glinting in afternoon light. Registration desks bustle with fighters. Water Divination awaits at floor 200—the threshold where aura separates the trained from the broken.
Heavens Arena.storyStart: Heavens Arena is overwhelming on first sight. The structure dominates the skyline—a vertical maze of polished stone and gleaming metal fixtures that seem to drink in light. The exterior bears plaques engraved with the names of legendary fighters, arranged by floor. Near the base, contemporary names cluster; as your eyes rise, the inscriptions become older, the fonts stranger. The main entrance is a sweeping circular opening, its interior as vast as a cathedral. Inside, the air thrums with the ambient sound of distant combat—echoes of fists striking flesh, the roar of crowds filtering down from upper tiers, the clang of weapons. The ground-level Registration Lobby is a study in organized chaos. Countless fighters move through the space, most of them young, lean, and carrying visible scars. Registration desks line one wall, each staffed by bureaucratic professionals who accept money and contracts with mechanical precision. A registration fee exists, an entry contract must be signed, and then fighters are directed to the Lower Floors to begin the climb. You observe the other new arrivals: some carry military bearing, others are street-fighters with predatory eyes, a few are scholars or travelers seeking something they cannot name. A woman at one registration desk accepts payment from a muscular fighter, then points casually toward the fighter elevator. She seems utterly unimpressed by a physique that took years to develop. "Floor 200," she says, "is where Nen separates the masters from the dead." This is where the rumors solidify into certainty. Nen is real. You've heard it whispered by candidates in the Exam. Here, at Heavens Arena, fighters speak about it openly—techniques that defy anatomy, aura visible around skilled combatants, a baptism of pain that transforms the untrained into something new. The Lower Floors visible through transparent partitions are already imposing—the combat galleries are filled with brutality that suggests a level of violence far beyond street-level brawling. But floor 200... the fighters speak of it with a reverence reserved for holy sites. You must reach it. You must pass it. Your fingers tremble slightly as you register your name.
Heavens Arena.questGenerationGuidance: The Heavens Arena arc is the canonical Nen-learning start. The primary quest (Climb to the 200th Floor) guides players through progressive tournament victories, with floor difficulty scaling according to player power. Floor 200 is the explicit rite of passage: an encounter with a Nen user (often Hisoka) that forces the player to confront the reality of aura-based combat. Wing, a veteran Nen teacher, appears as an optional but crucial mentor who teaches the fundamentals (Ten, Ren, Water Divination). His philosophy emphasizes respect for Nen's power and discipline over shortcuts. The secondary quest (The Teacher's Stake) rewards alignment with Wing's values and provides structured Nen education. Lower-floor encounters should introduce cast members (Zushi, Kastro, other fighters) and establish the arena's brutal culture. The atmosphere should be one of genuine danger—fighters here are talented and willing to inflict serious injury for victory.

Yorknew Auction Season.name: Yorknew Auction Season
Yorknew Auction Season.description: September in Yorknew City—the streets are alive with wealth, intrigue, and hidden danger. Underground auctions beckon. The Phantom Troupe's shadow looms unseen. The scarlet eyes of genocide circle through black markets like currency.
Yorknew Auction Season.storyStart: Yorknew City transforms during auction season. The glittering skyline intensifies, if such a thing were possible. The Southernpiece Auction House, already an architectural marvel, becomes the epicenter of a global convergence. Merchants, collectors, assassins, mafia families, and Hunters arrive in waves, their arrival marked by the visible expansion of private security details and the opening of luxury hotels that stand empty the rest of the year. The city's official face is ostentatious wealth and polite conduct. The streets pulse with traffic—exotic vehicles, personal security teams walking in coordinated patterns, negotiators speaking in quiet tones at sidewalk cafés. The official auction is public spectacle and enormous transaction volume; security is tight but visible. Beneath this surface lies the true market: the Underground Auction Hall, accessible only to vetted buyers, where artifacts of immeasurable value change hands in conditions of absolute secrecy. The air carries an electric anxiety. The Ten Dons' families have arrived. The Nostrade family—recently elevated on the strength of their daughter Neon's prophetic ability—moves through the upper echelons of society with new confidence. But there are whispers. Something feels wrong. The underworld intelligence networks are unusually tense. There are reports of the Phantom Troupe in the city, though no one can confirm sightings. The Troupe's history is a matter of public record: thirteen masked killers who destroyed the Kurta clan five years ago and scattered, their individual identities protected by secrecy and distance. They are spoken of with fear in mafia circles. If they are here, in Yorknew, during auction season, the implications are catastrophic. You've been retained for multiple purposes: security, acquisition, reconnaissance. Or perhaps you arrived seeking something specific—a treasure said to circulate through the underground market, a connection to your past, a thread to pull that might unravel a conspiracy. The city glitters. Beneath its surface, violence waits.
Yorknew Auction Season.questGenerationGuidance: The Yorknew arc is fundamentally political. Players may serve multiple factions: Zoldyck assassins hired for Ten Don protection, Hunters investigating the black market, mafia retainers securing goods, or independent treasure-hunters. The Phantom Troupe's massacre occurs mid-arc as a story event, forcing narrative improvisation. Kurapika's vendetta thread weaves through, introducing moral complexity—does the player help his revenge, or pursue neutral profit? The discovery of Scarlet Eyes in the market triggers the secondary quest (The Scarlet Market), offering players the opportunity to engage with black-market intrigue, dealer networks, and collector politics. Chrollo's Judgment Chain sealing him should occur naturally within the arc—a pivotal moment that reshapes power dynamics. The Troupe members should be dangerous, mysterious, and morally ambiguous; they are not villains, but predators with their own agendas.

Greed Island.name: Greed Island
Greed Island.description: The legendary Nen-construct game island materializes around you. In your hand: a ring and a Book. Spell cards lie waiting. Bombers farm players. And somewhere in this digital prison lies the Accompany card—the key to meeting your father.
Greed Island.storyStart: Arrival is disorienting. One moment, you stood in a facility handing over payment or being smuggled aboard a vessel. The next, reality shifts. You materialize on a vast grassland of perfect verdancy, beneath a sky of uncanny clarity. The grass is too perfectly uniform, too flawlessly green. Around you, thousands of other players materialize in synchronous waves—men, women, children, all marked with visible fatigue and confusion. Merchant tents are already erected, their vendors moving with algorithmic hospitality. "Welcome to Greed Island," a merchant says with an identical smile offered to every newcomer. A Tutorial Stone rises nearby, ancient and glowing, its surface inscribed with game rules in a language that somehow becomes comprehensible to you as you approach: spell cards, restricted items, the Book in your possession (which never fills, a bottomless container for your treasures), the Ring on your finger (your identification marker), the Accompany spell (the game's secret victory condition), item drops from defeated creatures, player-versus-player card acquisition, alliances and betrayals, and the mysterious Bomber trio terrorizing the wastes. The island extends in all directions to visible horizons. Your companions—if you have them—stand beside you, equally disoriented. The air carries the strange texture of a place that is simultaneously real and simulated, concrete yet somehow incorrect in ways you cannot quite articulate. Some players begin shouting questions at the merchants, who answer with perfect patience and no new information. Others immediately begin running inland, driven by instinct or greed. The Arrival Plain stretches vast and seemingly eternal. In the distance, you can glimpse structures—a town (Antokiba), forests, mountains, the outlines of adventure and danger both masked and obvious. In your inventory: your ring, your book, the clothes on your back, and whatever you managed to bring or smuggle aboard. Around you, 10,000 other players are simultaneously asking themselves: What is this place? How do we survive it? And most crucially: how do we escape?
Greed Island.questGenerationGuidance: The Greed Island arc is a training gauntlet disguised as a game. The primary quest (Clear Greed Island) guides card collection and alliance politics. The Bomber trio (Genthru, Sub, Bara) provide the midgame antagonist, forcing players to choose between farming cards in dangerous territory or alliance-building to survive. Biscuit Krueger appears as a recruiter and secret powerhouse trainer whose training montages teach Nen mastery through necessity. The secondary quest (The Dodgeball King) offers a final trial against Razor's Nen-beast devils—a test of teamwork and creative Nen application. The game's atmosphere should be surreal and mechanical—NPCs are sophisticated but subtly artificial; the landscape is magnificent but clearly constructed. Hisoka's presence should be felt without constant confrontation. The Accompany spell completion (meeting Kite) bridges to Arc 6 naturally. Nen baseline: Practitioner-Adept.

The Chimera Ant Crisis.name: The Chimera Ant Crisis
The Chimera Ant Crisis.description: At the NGL border checkpoint, something is terribly wrong. The green hills beyond pulse with an ominous wrongness. Kite stands beside you, ancient and exhausted. The quarantine gate closes behind you. Welcome to the world's darkest hour.
The Chimera Ant Crisis.storyStart: The NGL Border Checkpoint is a monument to isolation—high stone walls, minimal ceremony, guards with eyes like stones. The contrast between outside (temperate Mitene Union lands) and inside (bucolic, impossibly green, disturbingly quiet) is sharp enough to feel physical. Kite stands beside you if your journey has crossed paths with his expedition, or you have arrived independently seeking entry. Either way, the atmosphere is catastrophic. Kite's presence—ancient, exhausted, carrying the weight of terrible knowledge—suffuses the moment with dread. He has been investigating the isolation zone for months. What he found has broken him. The quarantine gate behind you closes with finality. There is no exit now save through. Ahead lies NGL's interior: villages that should contain people, fields that should show signs of habitation, and an ominous absence of sound. The green hills rise gently, beautiful and wrong. The sky above is perfectly clear, yet the light seems to carry a faint distortion, as if refracted through an invisible membrane. Kite speaks in a measured tone: "The colony extends farther than initial reports suggested. Humanoid soldiers, squad leaders, intelligence that adapts and improves. If the Queen has laid eggs—if there is a King—we are already defeated." The weight of this statement hangs. The other hunters on your team (if you have formed one) exchange looks. This is not a treasure hunt. This is not a Hunt. This is something else entirely. In the distance, barely perceptible, you hear a sound: not quite animal, not quite insect, something that triggers primal anxiety in your nervous system. The Investigation quest looms—players must traverse from the border through the interior, discovering the nest's extent, participating in guerrilla operations, and eventually joining or opposing the palace invasion. This arc is the violence ceiling. People you know will die. You may die. Victory, if it comes, will demand sacrifice.
The Chimera Ant Crisis.questGenerationGuidance: The Chimera Ant arc is the campaign's violence ceiling and thematic core. The primary quest (The NGL Incursion) is fundamentally about investigation transitioning into warfare. Early encounters emphasize reconnaissance and the growing horror as the colony's scope becomes apparent. Kite's death is a pivotal moment—heroes die here, unexpectedly and brutally. The secondary quest (Hearts of the Colony) offers emotional counterweight through encounters with human-memory ants (Colt, Ikalgo, Meleoron) who struggle between loyalty to the colony and their former humanity. The Royal Guards and Meruem are Master-tier mythic NPCs whose power redefines the campaign baseline. The palace invasion is coalition-effort; players are contributors, not commanders. Gon's catastrophic transformation (sacrificial vow → adult Gon, one-shot Pitou → comatose collapse) is the arc's emotional climax. This arc teaches that victory demands sacrifice, and that the world does not revolve around the player's story. Nen baseline: Adept.

The 13th Chairman Election.name: The 13th Chairman Election
The 13th Chairman Election.description: Netero's will is read aloud. The Zodiacs convene. Twelve of the world's strongest hunters begin an election circus that will reshape the Association itself. A boy dying in a hospital. A wish-granter hidden in a vault. The future crystallizes.
The 13th Chairman Election.storyStart: The Hunter Association HQ's Election Hall is configured for assembly. The Zodiacs—twelve of the world's most powerful hunters, each bearing an animal codename, each a legend in their own right—file into the chamber. Chairman Netero is dead, his will read by Beans (a subordinate so minor most hunters never knew she existed). The election rules are byzantine and theatrical, designed by Netero himself as a final jest: candidates are nominated and elected through multiple rounds involving games, popularity contests, and strategic voting. The entire process will take weeks. The absurdity is intentional. Pariston, the Rat, is magnificent and terrible—a man of immense power and unmaskable motive. He appears to be playing pure game-theory, orchestrating chaos for amusement or some deeper agenda no one can divine. Ging, the Boar—who revealed himself as Gon's father—carries his own mysteries. Kurapika and Leorio, newly elevated to Zodiac rank, represent the old guard's succession. The election proceedings are public spectacle layered over private machinations. You are present for multiple reasons: direct political interest (perhaps you are a Hunter yourself, seeking influence), personal connection (Gon lies comatose in Harbview Hospital, his Nen spent in a vow that nearly killed him), or factional loyalty (the Zodiacs command networks, and some are seeking allies). The atmosphere oscillates between theatre and genuine danger. These hunters have fought in wars. Several have survived encounters with Nen users of truly mythic power. They are not playing games, even as they pretend to. Killua races against time—his companion Gon is dying, and only Alluka, the legendary wish-granter sealed away in the Zoldyck vault, can save him. This parallel arc gives emotional weight to the political farce. The election determines the Association's next direction; Killua's race determines Gon's fate. Both converge.
The 13th Chairman Election.questGenerationGuidance: The Election arc is primarily political rather than combat-focused. The primary quest (The 13th Chairman Election) navigates election politics, surviving Pariston's machinations, and witnessing institutional power shifts. Leorio's symbolic punch (his vote surge) should reward moral clarity in a morally ambiguous system. The secondary quest (A Wish for a Life) is intimate—a race to find Alluka before Illumi, managing Nanika's escalating wish prices, and confronting family obligation versus friendship loyalty. Nanika should remain mysterious—her nature as a Gas-Life form from the Dark Continent is never explained, even in canon. Alluka/Nanika introduces player choice with permanent consequences (what price is acceptable? what does Gon become post-healing?). The arc teaches that institutional power is often comedy, that strength of character matters more than combat ability, and that the personal and political are inseparable. Nen baseline: Adept-Master.

The Dark Continent Voyage.name: The Dark Continent Voyage
The Dark Continent Voyage.description: Embarkation day on the Black Whale—a 200,000-passenger vessel sailing toward the Dark Continent. Fourteen princes begin a Succession War beneath the surface. Hisoka and the Phantom Troupe hunt one another. The world's greatest mysteries wait beyond Lake Mobius. Beyond that point lies only open sea and the unknown.
The Dark Continent Voyage.storyStart: The Black Whale is a floating civilization. At 200,000 passengers, it is larger than most cities. The ship rises in tiers—each tier a different world. Tier 1 contains royal quarters of opulent grandeur, where princes command Nen-beast guardians and plot each other's deaths beneath diplomatic courtesy. Tier 3 houses soldiers, scholars, and support staff. Tier 4 contains cargo, crew quarters, and the imprisoned. Above decks, the open expanse of Lake Mobius stretches to visible horizons. The water is dark—not black, but profoundly deep, suggesting abyssal depths and unknown inhabitants. Embarkation day carries the electric tension of departure. Thousands of people boarding simultaneously creates controlled chaos—security checks, cargo manifests, final preparations. You are aboard for multiple possible reasons: as part of Beyond Netero's expedition team, as a royal guard for one of the princes, as a Hunter fulfilling contracts, as a Phantom Troupe member hunting Hisoka (who recently self-revived after his fight with Chrollo), or as someone seeking passage to the unknowable continent beyond. The political situation is tense beneath surface civility. The Kakin Empire has recently joined the V5 nations, forming the V6. The succession war among the fourteen princes is a matter of public knowledge—it is the empire's official mechanism for determining the new ruler. Nen beasts—parasitic guardians born from vows, incomprehensible in their mechanics—are bound to each prince and follow rules that will be discovered, not stated. Multiple factions operate aboard: the Zodiacs conducting intelligence operations, Kurapika guarding Woble (Prince 14), the Phantom Troupe hunting Hisoka (who murdered two members, and they want revenge or his death), various alliance networks among the princes' supporters. The ship itself becomes a political arena—assassination attempts are frequent, subtle, and deadly. Above all hangs the promise of the Dark Continent. Beyond Lake Mobius lies territory unmapped, inhabited by beings that defy known biology, home to calamities that exceed even Meruem's power. Few who venture beyond the landing zone return unchanged. Many do not return at all. The voyage is simultaneously politics, war, mystery, and the approach of something vast and incomprehensible.
startingQuests: A8-The Voyage of the Black Whale
The Dark Continent Voyage.questGenerationGuidance: Arc 8 is the open-ended sandbox with maximum player agency. The primary quest (The Voyage of the Black Whale) emphasizes survival, alliance-building, and personal goal pursuit rather than a singular objective. Nen beasts are incomprehensible threats that defy tier, teaching that power is not universal. The Succession War's outcomes are EXTRAPOLATED—the manga is incomplete, so narrator discretion shapes which princes survive, which alliances hold, and whether the Dark Continent is reached intact. The secondary quest (Bodyguard to the Forgotten Queen) offers protection mechanics without direct combat solutions; success is measured by keeping Woble and Oito alive, maintaining autonomy, and reaching the Dark Continent with dignity. The arc emphasizes that the world persists beyond player control—they influence outcomes, not determine them. The Five Calamities should remain largely mysterious. The Dark Continent landing is described with uncertainty and speculative tone—the world-builders have not fully charted what lies there, and the narrator should reflect that mystery rather than impose certainty. An explicit lore tag must note the extrapolated content: 'Beyond the published manga, this story is open sea—outcomes are speculative continuation.' This arc teaches acceptance of ambiguity and player agency within constrained systems. Nen baseline: Master.
